STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no inner bowl wall. Square flat plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are 20-30 cm. This plate looks medium-large, about a standard dinner plate size, so roughly 24-26 cm across.
b) Reference cue: the sausages are about 3 cm in diameter. Across the plate width, the plate spans about 8 sausage-widths, which gives roughly 24 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm, so area = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Sausage (smoked/cooked sausage pieces): 6 visible rounds. Some are partly hidden under the eggs, so count about 6 items at roughly 25 g each (each about 2.5 cm diameter, 1.5 cm thick). Grams ≈ 6 x 25 = 150 g... to be conservative, treat as 5 rounds visible plus one hidden: 6 x 22 g ≈ 130 g.
- White scrambled/fluffy egg (the pale curds, looks like egg whites or cooked egg whites with some yolk): footprint about 20% of plate = 125 cm². Average thickness about 1.0 cm (a flat-ish layer with some mounding). Volume ≈ 125 ml x 1.0 = 125 ml... using a mound average of about 1.5 cm peak-to-average, I take ~1.2 cm average: 150 ml x 1.0 = 150 g.
- Yellow scrambled egg: footprint about 18% = 113 cm², average thickness about 1.5 cm (mound). Volume ≈ 170 ml x 0.8 = 136 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer under the items beyond the plate surface itself. No extra items added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Sausage: about 300 kcal/100 g (cooked smoked sausage).
- Egg white / cooked egg mix: about 150 kcal/100 g (white curds, lean).
- Scrambled whole egg (yellow): about 150 kcal/100 g (with butter/oil, roughly 160-180; use 170).

Totals: sausage ≈ 130 g, white egg ≈ 150 g, yellow scrambled egg ≈ 136 g, total ≈ 416 g.
